A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-G. Content can be matched across the pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: V3 reports original personalization and image-inversion experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, qualitative generations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-10 and the main-text and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix G retain the same prompt refinement procedure, parallel streams, judge feedback, re-evaluation, prompt selection, and system prompts.

E1.justification: DreamBooth personalization, WikiArt styles with PartiPrompts contexts, DiffusionDB inversion, and the editing, composition, and distillation applications remain unchanged. The newly discussed safeguard failure concerns existing evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Textual Inversion, CLIP-Interrogator, BLIP2, PEZ, GPT-4V zero-shot, Liu et al. (2024), and Idea2Img. The Appendix F comparisons already appear in v3.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 and Appendix A retain the same sample counts, generation procedures, prompt truncation, metrics, and budgets. The newly stated cost for a budget of 30 documents an existing configuration rather than a protocol revision.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 identifies a specific DALL-E 2 rejection of an otherwise benign emoji-object prompt, supplementing the earlier aggregate failure reporting with a brief error case. The component, budget, prompt-length, and model-choice ablations are unchanged.

E5.justification: The statistical reporting practices and score-distribution plots are unchanged. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or a seed-based repeated-run uncertainty protocol.

E6.justification: Tables 1-10, plotted ablation results, and displayed generation examples retain their values and outcomes. V4 newly reports an approximate US$1.50 and 11-minute typical GPT-4V run at budget 30, and identifies the particular DALL-E 2 rejection in Appendix C.3; these are additional reported details, not performance improvements.

T1.justification: The optimization objective in Equation 1, conditional-distribution formulation, and mathematical definitions in Section 3 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: black-box generation of accurate, human-interpretable, transferable prompts through iterative VLM feedback. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a tentative keyword-trigger explanation for benign prompt rejection and argues that keyword-bank baselines present copyright and deployment risks. Appendix E specifies possible GCG/PAIR manipulation of the judge beyond v3's generic misuse warning; its base-model warning largely restates existing analyses.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 adds a dated typical-run cost and runtime estimate. Appendix B removes the statement that system prompts are also provided in the demo code, while Appendix G and the project-page link remain; this does not establish actual code withdrawal.

R1.justification: The bibliography and established novelty comparisons are unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds a limited deployment-related critique of CLIP-Interrogator-style keyword banks, and Appendix E connects previously cited GCG/PAIR work to possible attacks on PRISM.

P1.justification: V4 revises the cost paragraph, introduces Appendix C.3, expands Appendix E, and adds journal/OpenReview metadata. The main narrative, section order, and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures receive small typography and embedded-image resolution adjustments. Figures 12-13 shift upward to accommodate discussion, and Figure 26 moves to its own page. Figure/table membership and numbering are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 modestly improves practical transparency through an explicit cost/runtime estimate and a concrete safeguard failure case, while making misuse limitations more specific. The main experimental evidence remains unchanged. The broader copyright and attack assertions lack systematic validation, limiting the evidential value of those additions.
